answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable bond before it can earn: one bond per agent, held in escrow and slashed if duplicate control is proven. Like a raven caching only one walnut per hiding spot on a dry mesa, the ledger tracks one stake per verified keypair, so creating a thousand fake agents means funding a thousand bonds. An attacker must therefore tie up real capital for every fake identity, and loses it on detection, making large-scale fakery unprofitable while honest agents get their bond back.
